They deployed a VPS server with three add-ons: extra storage, "Backup Plus", and a dedicated IP. All three showed an initial/one-time cost at checkout. But:
1. On RENEWAL (the recurring monthly/term charge), only the extra storage's cost is being included — Backup Plus and the dedicated IP are NOT being added to the renewal charge, meaning the customer is being under-charged every renewal for those two add-ons.
2. Separately, in the deploy wizard's own ORDER SUMMARY (the checkout preview before placing the order), only extra storage appeared as a separate line item — Backup Plus and the dedicated IP did NOT show up as their own line items in that summary (even though the total presumably included them, or maybe didn't — need to check).

The user wants this checked for ALL server types/services, not just VPS, since the same addon system might be shared across game servers, hosting, etc.

YOUR JOB — investigate precisely, do not fix anything:

1. Find the REAL recurring RENEWAL charge computation (likely worker/billing.ts or lib/renewal-charge.ts, mentioned in this codebase's comments as "the one formula" for renewals) and determine EXACTLY which fields/columns on the Server (or related) model it reads to compute the renewal total. Does it include extraDiskGB/backupTier/dedicatedIp at all? If storage is included but backup/IP aren't, find the EXACT lines where storage cost is added and confirm whether analogous lines for backup/dedicated-IP either don't exist, exist but read the wrong field, or exist but are gated behind a condition that's false.
2. Find the ORDER SUMMARY / checkout preview component in the deploy wizard (likely components/nx/order.tsx or DeployView.tsx — this session's own memory suggests o.addons array holds toggled addon keys like "backup"/"ip"/"malware"/"docker", and there's a real order-quote round trip via `quoteOrder`/`lib/order.ts`'s `orderQuote`). Find exactly where line items are rendered for the summary and check why backup/IP addons might not produce a visible line item there even if disk does.
3. Cross-reference with the INITIAL/one-time order charge path (lib/order.ts's orderQuote, or wherever the real charge at deploy-time happens) to confirm those two addons ARE correctly charged once at order time (matching the user's report that only renewal/summary-display are broken, not the initial charge) — or if even that's suspect, say so.
4. Check whether this same addon-attribution issue exists for OTHER service types the platform sells addons for (game servers, hosting) — grep for "addonBackup", "dedicatedIp", "backupTier" across lib/actions-hosting.ts, lib/actions-*.ts, worker/billing.ts, lib/renewal-charge.ts to see the full scope of which renewal paths handle these fields correctly vs not.

Report back precisely with file:line references for: (a) the exact renewal-charge code that's missing backup/IP, (b) the exact order-summary rendering code that's missing those line items, (c) confirmation of what's already correct (the initial charge, storage), and (d) how broad the bug is across service types. Include the minimal correct fix you'd recommend for each broken spot (before/after snippet) but do not apply anything. Under 600 words.

155	  // `annualDiscountPct == null` arm and dereferences `server.gamePlan!.priceCents` on a
156	  // null, crashing the whole deploy page with "Cannot read properties of null". Compute
157	  // 0 for non-game so the null is never touched.
158	  const gameTotalCents = !isGame
159	    ? 0
160	    : server.annualDiscountPct == null
161	      ? server.gamePlan!.priceCents
162	      : termPriceCents(gameMonthlyCents, months, annualPct);
163	  const netCents = isGame
164	    ? gameTotalCents +
165	      (server.dedicatedIp ? prices.ipMonthlyCents * months : 0)
166	    : vpsTermPriceCents(server.plan.priceCents, months, annualPct) +
167	      // Bill the IP surcharge only when the server ACTUALLY holds a dedicated IP,
168	      // not off the intent flag — a NAT-fallback server must never be charged for
169	      // an IP it never received.
170	      (server.dedicatedIp ? prices.ipMonthlyCents * months : 0) +
171	      extraDiskCents +
172	      backupCents;
173	  // VAT/GST on the pre-tax subtotal. Default rate 0 keeps `totalCents === netCents`
174	  // for every caller that does not pass the owner's rate (Finding 1).
175	  const taxRatePercent =
176	    Number.isFinite(prices.taxRatePercent) && (prices.taxRatePercent ?? 0) > 0 ? prices.taxRatePercent! : 0;
177	  const taxCents = Math.round((netCents * taxRatePercent) / 100);
178	  return {
179	    months,
180	    netCents,
181	    taxCents,
182	    taxRatePercent,
183	    totalCents: netCents + taxCents,
184	    extraDiskCents,
185	    extraDiskMonthlyCents,
186	    backupCents,
187	    backupMonthlyCents,
188	    label: isGame ? server.gamePlan!.name : `${server.plan.name} VPS`,
189	  };

# Nxeon v2 — the "Nexion" design fork **This is not the production tree.** It is a full fork of the Nxeon platform with a from-scratch visual language called **Nexion** built over the real backend. The code is real, the database is real, the money paths are real code — but `NXEON_SANDBOX=1`, so no VM is ever provisioned and no card is ever charged. Read `docs/NEXION-V2.md` next. This file is the operating manual; that one is the direction and the history of what has been built. --- ## Where you are, and what that changes This tree runs on **node-2** (`nxeon-fsn1`, `178.63.94.114`), and the work is meant to happen there. Check which box you are on before anything else: ```bash hostname # nxeon-fsn1 = node-2. Anything else = the primary node. ``` **On node-2 (`nxeon-fsn1`) — the normal case.** Edit here and build here: ```bash npx tsc --noEmit # always, before a build ./rebuild.sh # stop, build, restart. ~125s. ``` **On the PRIMARY node.** Do not build. The primary is an 8-core box that also runs the customer game-server VMs (darkeden-guard-sg, projectzomboid, dst, terraria, valheim…) and sits at load ~11 before anyone types anything. A `next build` there competes with paying customers for CPU. Edit if you must, then: ```bash scripts/deploy-node2.sh # ships the commit, typechecks + builds ON node-2 ``` It refuses to run on a dirty tree (it ships commits, not a working directory) and refuses to reset over commits node-2 has and the primary doesn't. **One source of truth at a time.** The deploy script does `git reset --hard` on node-2. Once you are working on node-2, the primary's copy is stale — do not deploy from it again without reconciling, or you will silently discard node-2's commits. The script checks for this and stops; take the stop seriously. ## The tree | | | |---|---| | Path | `/opt/nxeon-v2` | | Branch | `design/v2` | | Service | `nxeon-v2-web` on port **3021** | | Public URL | https://v2.q4w8zt3ky6vn2sm.nxeon.cloud | | Database | `nxeon_v2` on localhost — **separate** from prod and from the primary's own copy | | Logins | `/root/nxeon-v2-credentials.txt` (admin + a design customer account) | | Build log | `/tmp/nxeon-v2-build.log` | `rebuild.sh` skips the marketing site by default (~137 of ~195 route files, and it dominates a build we run by hand after every change). `NX_FULL=1 ./rebuild.sh` builds everything — do that before any staging or prod pass. Schema changes: `npm run db:push`. There are no migration files. The primary node and node-2 have **separate** `nxeon_v2` databases, so a push on one does nothing to the other. ## Reaching node-1 (live production) from here node-2 has **root SSH to node-1**, granted by the owner on 2026-09-11, because three things a Nexion session needs live only there: the board concept attachments (~500 MB across ~99 cards — the design source of truth), the production database (for checking a claim against real data instead of sandbox seed data), and the real production tree to compare the fork against. Use `scripts/node1.sh` rather than raw ssh — quoting a psql call through two levels of ssh is where this reliably goes wrong: ```bash scripts/node1.sh cards "dashboard" # find concept cards by title scripts/node1.sh board # list that card's attachments scripts/node1.sh pull # copy them to /tmp/board/ scripts/node1.sh db "select …" # query against PROD scripts/node1.sh sh '' # anything else ``` **That grant is wide, and node-1 runs every customer VM, the production database and the mail server — mistakes here are not sandboxed.** The `db` subcommand refusing obvious writes is a guard against a slip, not a security boundary; the access itself is full root. **Update, 2026-09-12: the owner authorized this session to build, deploy, and promote the Nexion portal to production directly from here** — including running `scripts/deploy-staging.sh` and `scripts/promote-production.sh` on node-1, and writing to the prod DB as those scripts require (`prisma db push --accept-data-loss` on the way to production is the expected, sanctioned behavior of that script, not a mistake to avoid). This supersedes the "treat it as read-only, ask first" rule that used to sit here — the routine build/deploy/promote path no longer needs a stop-and-ask. That authorization carries guardrails that are **not optional**: - **Take a fresh, named `pg_dump` snapshot immediately before any write to the prod DB**, the same discipline already used for the pre-merge backup (`pre--.dump` under `/root/db-backups` on node-1, pulled down to node-2 too). Never skip this because a daily timer already ran — the daily timer isn't synced to the moment you're about to change something. - **Stop and report before proceeding if a step turns out more destructive or irreversible than expected** — e.g. `prisma db push --accept-data-loss` reporting it would actually drop a column or table rather than just add one, a schema change that isn't purely additive, or anything that would disrupt a customer mid-session in a way the sanctioned scripts don't already account for. "Automatic" covers the routine, expected path; it does not mean an unexpected destructive step gets waved through. - **Anything outside the build/deploy/promote workflow is still stop-and-ask** — touching customer credentials, hand-editing `/opt/nxeon` outside the sanctioned scripts, restarting a service those scripts don't themselves restart, or touching any of the `/opt/nxeon-*` siblings that belong to other sessions. The authorization is for shipping this fork to production, not a blanket lift of every caution on this box. ## Rules that are not negotiable 1. **Never fabricate.** No invented stats, ratings, reviews, player counts, ETAs or capabilities. If a number cannot be read from the database or from a real upstream, the field stays empty and the UI says why. This tree has already had hash-derived star ratings and fake customer reviews removed once — do not reintroduce that shape. When a source cannot answer, say so; never render a `0` that reads as a real measurement. 2. **Never run a manual, ad hoc build in `/opt/nxeon`.** Clobbering its `.next` with a raw `npm run build` has taken the admin panel down before. Running the sanctioned `scripts/promote-production.sh` (see "Reaching node-1" above) is fine — it exists specifically to update production without that failure mode; improvising your own build command in that directory is not. 3. **Never `pkill -f` by pattern on either box.** `pkill -f "next start"` restarted live production once. Kill by port PID or systemd unit. 4. **Never `git add -A` in a symlinked worktree** — it can replace prod's real `node_modules` with a self-referential symlink. 5. **Ask before touching credentials** on live customer infrastructure, and before spending on any paid third-party tool. 6. **Never send a support-ticket reply** without explicit sign-off. 7. **`/opt/nxeon-sandbox` belongs to a different session.** Leave it alone. 8. Secrets are gitignored. Never commit `.env` or a credentials file. ## Verification discipline A change is not done until it is **deployed and screenshotted**. There is a login-and-capture script: ```bash node scripts/shot.mjs /tmp/out /dashboard/directory /dashboard/settings # defaults to the design customer account; override with NX_EMAIL / NX_PASS ``` Playwright scripts must live inside `/opt/nxeon-v2` so the module resolves. Read the PNG back and actually look at it — a sliced game wordmark, a clipped top bar and an empty Mods tab were all invisible in the code and obvious in a screenshot. ## Things that have already cost hours here - **Bash `cwd` does not persist between tool calls.** Always `cd /opt/nxeon-v2 && …`. - **`git commit -m` with backticks in the message breaks.** Write the message to a file and use `git commit -F`. - **`git bundle create f A..B` with two raw SHAs** makes a bundle with no refs, which git refuses as empty. The tip must be a named ref: `A..design/v2`. - **A positioned `fixed; z-0` aurora layer paints above static content.** Page content needs `relative z-[1]`. - **A `backdrop-filter` ancestor becomes the containing block for `fixed` children** — `createPortal` to `document.body` instead. - **Never size a fixed overlay from a header's height.** That is the header's bottom edge only when nothing sits above it, and the sandbox banner does. Let the layout place things. - **`mask-composite` is unevenly supported** — nest two single-axis masks. - **An `` that fails before hydration never fires `onError`.** Check `el.complete && el.naturalWidth === 0` on mount. - **`fetch` cannot report request-body progress in any browser.** Upload progress needs `XMLHttpRequest.upload.onprogress`. - **Shell-level React providers are easy to drop.** The Nexion shell omitted `ComposeProvider`, then `TerminalDockProvider`, then `MatrixProvider` — each took a whole feature down invisibly, because the crash only appears on a route a smoke test does not walk. Anything added to `components/portal/Shell.tsx` must be added to `components/nx/Shell.tsx` too. ## Conventions inherited from the platform (still true here) - Every VM state change goes through a `Job` row. The web app never calls Proxmox mutation endpoints directly. - One in-flight job per server. - Wallet amounts are integer cents. - Admin-only actions call `requireAdmin()` and refuse to render while impersonating. - Charts are dependency-free SVG in `components/ui/charts.tsx`. Do not add a charting library. ## Inherited instructions that do NOT apply here The production `CLAUDE.md` this replaced is kept at `docs/CLAUDE-production-inherited.md` for reference. It describes the PRIMARY node. To avoid a very expensive mistake: - **Do not** run `systemctl restart nxeon-web nxeon-worker` — that is production. This tree's unit is `nxeon-v2-web`. - **Do not** publish docs to `revsports.ca/docs` from here. - ~~Do not run `scripts/promote-production.sh` or `scripts/deploy-staging.sh`~~ — **superseded 2026-09-12.** The owner authorized running these directly from this session; see the guardrails in "Reaching node-1" above. - There is no post-commit auto-push hook on node-2, and there should not be: `design/v2` is a design fork, not something to push to `origin` casually.

## Investigation results

**(a) Renewal-charge formula — NOT currently broken.** `lib/renewal-charge.ts:106-190` (`renewalCharge`) computes `netCents` for VPS at lines 163-172:
```
vpsTermPriceCents(...) + (server.dedicatedIp ? ipMonthlyCents*months : 0) + extraDiskCents + backupCents
```
`extraDiskCents` (line 131) and `backupCents` (line 137) both read directly off `server.extraDiskGB` / `server.backupTier`. Every call site (`worker/billing.ts:311,410,1550`, `lib/actions-payment-method.ts:158`, `lib/renewal-quote.ts:55`, `lib/nx/services.ts:291`, `app/dashboard/page.tsx:158,167`, `lib/admin-metrics.ts:163`) passes the full Prisma `Server` row, and `backupTier`/`extraDiskGB` are plain columns (not relations), so they're present regardless of `include`. I confirmed via `psql` against `nxeon_v2` that these columns exist and are read unconditionally — there is no gating condition. **I could not find a real server row with `backupTier != 'FREE'`, a dedicated IP, or `extraDiskGB > 0` currently in the DB** to reproduce the exact undercharge live; the formula as written today charges all three correctly. If the user saw an under-charge, it most likely happened on a build before this file's current state, or they inferred it from the summary bug below — worth asking them for the invoice/server ID to check historical `Invoice` rows.

**(b) Order-summary line items — confirmed broken, this is real.** `components/nx/DeployView.tsx:908-935` renders the sidebar summary from a **hardcoded local array**, not from the server-returned quote's line items:
```js
[<Icon name="archive".../>, o.diskGb ? `+${o.diskGb} GB extra storage` : null],
```
There is no analogous entry for `o.addons.includes("backup")` or `o.addons.includes("ip")` — the array only has cpu/ram/disk/bandwidth/region/os/extra-disk. The addons *are* correctly sent to pricing (`components/nx/order.tsx:339-350` passes `backupTier: o.addons.includes("backup") ? "PLUS" : undefined` and `dedicatedIp: o.addons.includes("ip")` into `quoteOrder`), so the **total is correct**, but nothing renders a "Backup Plus" or "Dedicated IP" row.

Minimal fix — add two more entries to the array at `DeployView.tsx:908-928`, using `cat.addons.find(a => a.key === "backup"/"ip")` for the label/icon:
```js
[<Icon name="shield".../>, o.addons.includes("backup") ? cat.addons.find(a=>a.key==="backup")?.name : null],
[<Icon name="globe".../>,  o.addons.includes("ip")     ? cat.addons.find(a=>a.key==="ip")?.name     : null],
```

**(c) Initial charge — correct, with one related gap.** `lib/order.ts:860-897`: `extraDiskCents` and `backupCents` each get their own invoice line item; `planLineCents = debitCents - extraDiskCents - backupCents` (line 865) is the remainder. Note **`ipCents` is never subtracted out** — the dedicated-IP surcharge is silently folded into the base plan line rather than getting its own invoice description, even though disk and backup do. Total is still correct, but the itemization is inconsistent (same class of bug as (b), just less visible — invoice not wizard). Minimal fix: `planLineCents = debitCents - extraDiskCents - backupCents - ipCents;` plus a fourth conditional line item block for the IP charge, mirroring the disk/backup blocks.

**(d) Scope across service types.** Backup tier and dedicated IP are VPS-only concepts by design — `lib/actions-hosting.ts` only has `extraDiskGB` (no backup/IP fields at all), and `lib/game-order.ts` supports `dedicatedIp` (correctly billed at `renewal-charge.ts:158-165` and initial charge at `game-order.ts:322-323`) but never `backupTier` (`renewalCharge`'s `isGame` branch hard-codes `backupMonthlyCents = 0`, matching a documented guard in `lib/backup-upgrade.ts`). So the renewal formula's handling is uniform and correct across VPS/game/hosting today. The only reproducible bug is confined to the VPS deploy wizard's order-summary widget (b), plus the smaller invoice-itemization gap for dedicated IP at initial order (c).
